text:
Sam W: Heads-up — we plan to sunset the legacy sync client in both Python and TS SDKs in tonight's publish window (22:00 PT). Need owners for canary + rollback play, release notes line, and dist-tag pin strategy. @Maria L can you own the rollforward criteria?
Maria L: Ack. I can own. Quick Q: do we want a soft-deprecate first (dist-tag + deprecation banner) or immediate removal in the major?
Sam W: We'll remove in 2.0.0 (major) but do a soft-deprecate on the last 1.x before the big cut — dist-tag 'legacy' + banner in docs. Canary will be 2.0.0-canary.
Jon Q: I'll run the smoke suite. Focus tests: streaming, function-calls, sync->async migration surface. If any auth regressions or streaming failures show up, call for rollback.
Priya S: SRE plan: traffic-shift rollout: 1% (10m), 10% (20m), 100% if metrics stable. Alert thresholds: 2x error rate baseline or 20% latency p90 degradation = immediate rollback.
Sam W: Publish checklist (short):
```
- bump versions: py 2.0.0, ts 2.0.0
- npm publish --tag next-canary (for canary)
- python: build sdist & wheel, upload to test.pypi then twine to prod after canary
- update release-notes with migration snippet
- add deprecation banner on docs for legacy sync client
- create release PR with pinned examples
```
Sam W: exact commands I’ll run:
```
# TS canary
npm version 2.0.0-canary.0 --no-git-tag-version
npm publish --tag next-canary
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2.0.0-canary.0 next-canary
# PyPI build
python -m build
twine upload dist/* --repository pypi
```
Maria L: Rollback play (if canary fails or metrics breach):
- revert dist-tag: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.9.5 latest` and remove the canary tag
- for PyPI: publish a 1.9.6 patch and pin docs to 1.9.x examples; add a deprecation notice in the 2.0.0 release notes so customers know why we backfilled
- notify customers via #support and post in release notes channel
Jon Q: Criteria to flip from canary -> gradual rollout: no functional regressions in smoke + <1% increase in error rate + p50/p90 within 10% of baseline for 30m.
Priya S: Deploy-bot hooks: please include `--enable-canary-telemetry` flag so we can get granular traces. If deploy-bot sees >5 failing deploys it should stop and notify oncall.
devex-bot: @deploy-bot has permission to run `deploy canary` for channel devex. Use `/deploy canary --tag next-canary --autopause` to start.
deploy-bot: Scheduled: canary trigger at 1768001200 (22:00 PT). Will run smoke tests and report back.
Sam W: Release-notes blurb (draft): "We are removing the legacy sync client in 2.0.0. Please migrate to the async client — see migration guide snippet below. We are providing a soft-deprecation on 1.x with updated docs and a fallback patch for customers who need more time." :shipit:
Sam W: Migration snippet to include in docs:
```
# Python (sync->async)
from redwood import Client
# old sync usage
# client = Client(sync=True)
# new async usage
import asyncio
async def main():
    client = Client()
    await client.chat.create("Hello")
asyncio.run(main())
```
Maria L: Sounds good. Jon, Priya — if canary passes, we'll schedule staggered cutover window 00:30-02:00 PT tomorrow for full rollout. If anything suspicious appears during the 10%-100% shift we stop and revert to 1.9.x via dist-tag pin.
Jon Q: I'll be on-call for smoke and quick fix PRs.
Priya S: I'll open a short runbook in the incident docs and add alerting playbook entries.
Sam W: Last ask — include a short deprecation note in the changelog and call out exact removal date. I'll prepare the release PR now. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
